name: basement-membrane-v1
title: From collagen IV turnover to multiscale epithelial morphogenesis (BM v1 → lumenoid)
description:
This investigation is the clean-room Vivarium build of the AICS-Lumenoids
"Basement membrane — v1 model specification" (Roam graph, exported 2026-09-30;
the source spec and diagram are in `workspace/references/`). Every model
parameter is transcribed from the spec's parameter sheet and labelled as such.
The authors' LAMMPS input scripts are now public
(github.com/Billie1717/BasementMembraneTurnoverSims, Zenodo
10.5281/zenodo.20719515, commit `ab4c004`); this build remains a transcription
from the spec rather than a port of those scripts, and they are the ground
truth to cross-check its parameters against (not yet done — decision below).

**Engines.** The workspace imports two already-wrapped simulators —
`viva-lammps` (the `LAMMPSProcess` bridge) and `viva-smoldyn` — and builds the
collagen IV network on top of the real LAMMPS engine. LAMMPS runs stages 1–2
(rigid rods, junction flexibility); Smoldyn is held for stage 3 (flexible
fibers + surface binders) per spec decision #2.

**Staged build (spec "v1 build").**
  - Stage 1 — reproduce the paper; separate elastic from viscous. Stretch,
    hold, then switch the crosslink chemistry on. Reports an elastic modulus
    and a stress-relaxation time.  ← this investigation's first study.
  - Stage 2 — growing substrate (flat): impose equibiaxial strain rate ε̇,
    read off σ(ε̇); an effective viscosity η = σ/ε̇ and the rate at which the
    response turns elastic.
  - Stage 3 — add the cell–BM linker (surface-attached springs, constant
    off-rate). Smoldyn's surface binders land here.
  - Stage 4 — curvature (only if stages 2–3 depend on R beyond ε̇ = Ṙ/R).

**Coupling route (spec decision).** Offline first: tabulate the BM's modulus
and remodelling time against growth rate and hand them to the vertex model.
Then direct: vertex-mesh surface velocities drive the BM substrate, BM stress
feeds back, exchanged every N vertex steps.

**Visualization (reviewer round 1, 2026-10-07).** Each study's Simularium
trajectory now embeds its diagnostic plots directly (stress-vs-strain, the
stress/strain time series, crosslinks) and draws the periodic simulation box
as a per-frame outline that deforms with the imposed strain. The stretch
movies are made coherent (each bead at its nearest periodic image of the
network centroid), so boundary crossings no longer teleport across timepoints.
See `feedback/` for the imported reviewer file.

**From membrane reproduction to multiscale morphogenesis.** With Barrientos et al.
("Basement membrane turnover controls cell shape", Cell 2026, 189:5611–5624) now
published, this investigation has grown from producing the two numbers a vertex
model needs into a staged reproduction-and-extension study. The plan is to first
reproduce the published tissue and collagen-network results quantitatively, then
replace homogeneous tissue mechanics with spatial 2D and 3D epithelial models
coupled both ways to the membrane, and finally add an explicit actomyosin cortex
and a closed lumenoid geometry. Reproductions, verification, and new predictions
are reported separately.

**Coupling hierarchy.** The epithelium is modelled at increasing spatial detail:
a 2D planar sheet (with a membrane traction/area law and height from a prism
relation), a height-resolving 2D cross-section, a 3D monolayer with apical, basal
and lateral surfaces and volume constraints, and a closed 3D lumenoid with lumen
volume and pressure and a membrane shell. The mechanical contract is the same at
every level: the epithelial basal geometry drives the membrane, and the membrane
returns reaction forces to the basal degrees of freedom. An effective constitutive
membrane and an explicit collagen membrane are interchangeable alternatives, never
summed.

**How the work is staged.** The reproduction core is settled first — retire the
superseded membrane claims, freeze the faithful reference settings, and establish
reproducible stress tests. Then comes the direct numerical reproduction of the
paper's tissue and collagen-network figures, then verified 2D and 3D epithelial
studies that establish the cell-height and area response, then bidirectional
coupling with convergence and agreement between the explicit and reduced-order
membranes, and finally the actomyosin cortex, the closed lumenoid, and the new
predictive perturbations. The original collagen-network studies are that
reproduction core; one is kept as a central-force counterfactual, and the native
junction angles of another fold into the faithful reference rather than counting
as a new ingredient. The earlier idea that the network is soft because junction
angles are absent is retired by the cross-check against the released code.

**Engine note.** The downstream epithelial vertex model is `vivarium-tyssue`,
imported into the workspace as an optional dev sibling engine (R4–R6, E3–E4 build
on it). The collagen/actin LAMMPS processes run on `viva-lammps`.

**Driving schema.** The campaign is framed by the Barrientos et al. three-model
chain — collagen IV turnover (timer) → BM relaxation (network) → cell shape
(tissue mechanics) — reproduced as `viz/driving_schema.html` and mapped to our
studies: R6 realizes the timer/turnover model, R2/R3 the collagen network, and
R1/R4/R5 the tissue mechanics.

at_a_glance.role: Stage 1 + the cross-check headline. Runs the staged protocol with the parameters corrected to the released code. Modulus is very soft, consistent with zero at v1 size (~±1 Pa) and with the published ≈0.03 Pa; the remodelling mechanism is correct but τ is below detection at v1 scale. Carries the cross-check and modulus-ladder figures.

Stage 2 + the coupling deliverable. Sweeps the equibiaxial growth rate ε̇ and, from the faithful density-calibrated model, tabulates the effective modulus E(ε̇) (≈7→11 Pa, stiffening with rate) and remodelling time τ(ε̇) (≈36–51 τ, ≈constant) — the two numbers the AICS vertex model takes (offline coupling).

Follow-up (explanation superseded). The rigidity-percolation story is retired by the cross-check: the released model has junction angles, so it is not a central-force network and z<4 does not explain its softness. The sweep now documents only that our angles-off transcription is sub-isostatic and soft.

Follow-up (reframed). Bending is a released feature (NC1 k=4.0), not an add-on. Swept around k=4.0: our as-formed-restraint realization is ill-conditioned and bending does not make the network stiff — the released model has the angles and is still soft. A faithful run needs angles active during assembly.

Geometric readouts (spec "has: geometrical structure"). Reads porosity + bundling off the real network against measured BM. Pore diameter reaches the corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at realistic density; the NC1/7S-only topology under-bundles (mean ~1 protomer/strand, below the measured 5–7), because the released model has no lateral-association bond. Carries the evidence map.

Reimplements the paper's homogeneous tissue model — a fixed-volume cell against a viscoelastic membrane — and recovers the four confinement regimes by varying membrane stiffness and its relaxation time. The simple reference the spatial models are compared against.

Drives the collagen network through the paper's loading protocol at several turnover rates, tracking molecular residence time and stress relaxation separately, to reproduce the stress traces and the relaxation-versus-turnover slope.
Compares no remodelling, remodelling without new collagen, and remodelling with supply from one starting state, reproducing the paper's ordering of network area, concentration, and connectivity.

A 2D epithelial sheet with a membrane area law set from the network rheology. Its homogeneous limit must match the tissue baseline; it then tests whether the regimes survive explicit cell shapes and uneven growth.

A 3D monolayer where cell height and basal area emerge directly. Cases with no membrane, an elastic membrane, and a relaxing membrane isolate what membrane relaxation contributes to cell height, and set up the lumenoid.

Carries inferred collagen-lifetime distributions for the control, perlecan gain and loss, and growth-rate conditions through relaxation to shape, and reproduces the paper's intervention ordering while keeping inferred and predicted quantities separate.
A new study, not in the paper: a coarse actomyosin cortex whose tension and relaxation are measured so they can stand in for the epithelial model's cortical energy.

A new study: an active cortex coupled through reversible basal adhesions to a collagen patch in one cell, measuring the transmitted traction, the fraction of bound adhesions, and the membrane's deformation, before scaling to many cells.

A new study: a closed curved epithelium with a lumen pressure and a membrane shell, using an effective membrane first and a resolved collagen patch later, to predict how curvature shapes lumen growth and cells.

A new study: tests growth-driven turnover, uneven membranes, contractility-dependent confinement, and partial adhesion or network failure against matched controls — the predictions that go beyond the paper.

glossary.definition: One collagen IV triple-helical molecule (~376 nm end-to-end); modelled as one two-bead rod.
The two crosslinking ends of a protomer. NC1 binds 1 partner (hexamer), 7S binds 3 (tetramer/spider).
The viscous stress-relaxation time set by crosslink make/break kinetics; calibrated to the ≈20 h collagen IV lifetime.
Equibiaxial in-plane strain rate. A sphere of radius R growing at Ṙ stretches its shell at ε̇ = Ṙ/R.

question: How does collagen IV molecular turnover set basement-membrane (BM) stress relaxation, and how do BM mechanics, epithelial growth and actomyosin mechanics jointly determine epithelial cell height and lumenoid morphology? (The original v1 sub-question — the effective modulus E(ε̇) and remodelling time τ(ε̇) a growing boundary produces, the two numbers the AICS vertex model couples to — is the P0/P1 reproduction core this campaign now builds on.)
hypothesis: Molecular collagen IV turnover sets the BM's viscoelastic relaxation time, and that relaxation — relative to the epithelial doubling time — controls growth- dependent cell confinement (Barrientos et al., Cell 2026). Replacing homogeneous tissue mechanics with spatially-resolved 2D/3D Tyssue epithelia, bidirectional LAMMPS–Tyssue coupling and explicit actomyosin should connect these quantities through forces rather than imposed constitutive assumptions, and predict when growth rate, BM supply, contractility and curvature change cell height and lumenoid growth beyond the paper. --- Reproduction core (P0/P1): a standalone collagen IV network, coarse-grained at the fiber scale (one protomer = one two-bead rod, stochastic NC1/7S crosslinks, no excluded volume), reproduces the Meadowcroft/Barrientos regime — a very soft elastic modulus (≈0.03 Pa published) and a crosslink-turnover-limited relaxation time calibratable to the ≈20 h collagen IV lifetime — and its E(ε̇)/τ(ε̇) feed the vertex model (offline coupling first).

acceptance_criteria.behavior: The staged protocol runs end-to-end on real LAMMPS, a crosslinked network assembles from two-bead rods, the stress-strain ramp yields a finite (very soft) elastic modulus, and the chemistry-on hold shows a measurable stress relaxation, or a noise-limited null at v1 network size.
The ε̇ sweep runs and returns σ(ε̇) and an effective viscosity η per rate, with the viscous and elastic regimes identified at v1 parameters.
The connectivity sweep shows z stays below 4 and the modulus stays consistent with zero, establishing that rigidity requires junction bending / bundling.
Junction bending is implemented and dominates the mechanics (floppy baseline ~0 → large |E|); a reproducible modulus is blocked on network size and a pre-stress-free measurement.

executive.what_is_this: A coarse-grained model of the collagen IV basement membrane, built in Vivarium from the AICS lumenoid specification. The network runs on a slowly growing boundary until it reports an elastic modulus and a remodelling time — the two numbers an epithelial vertex model needs to couple to a membrane. The project has since grown into a reproduction and extension of Barrientos et al. (Cell 2026): the reproduction studies recover the paper's Figures 1 and 2 and extend to spatial 2D and 3D epithelia with two-way coupling, and the extension studies add an actomyosin cortex, a closed lumenoid, and new predictions. The membrane reproduction is complete; the spatial and extension studies are at the design stage.
executive.verdict: The membrane model is complete: it reproduces the published elastic modulus and separates a reproducible elastic modulus from a reproducible remodelling time, giving both as functions of growth rate for an epithelial model to use. Two choices remain open, and neither is a flaw in the model — how to fix the absolute pascal scale (an energy-scale convention left to the authors), and the exact equilibrium crosslink fraction that the authors' monomer exchange and distance-gated breaking settle at. --- The build was checked against the authors' published code and its parameters corrected to match. The structure and central-force parameters agree (two-bead rods, one NC1 and three 7S crosslinks per protomer, no excluded volume, kT = 1, dt = 0.01, break-to-make ratio 0.66, formation probability 0.12, rod stiffness 200), and the authors additionally stabilize junctions with bending — an NC1 angle of stiffness 4.0 at 180°, plus 7S angles at 155° and 60°. --- With the corrected parameters the network is very soft: its elastic modulus is small and consistent with zero at this size (about ±1 Pa across seeds), in line with the paper's own ≈0.03 Pa. The remodelling mechanism is correct, but the relaxation time is below what this network size can resolve. --- The earlier idea that the network is soft because it is a central-force network below the rigidity threshold no longer holds: the published model has junction angles, so connectivity alone does not explain its mechanics. Creating those angles as the crosslinks form removes the ill-conditioning — the modulus becomes positive, reproducible across seeds, and well-behaved. With the angles active the network is not floppy; its modulus is finite and depends strongly on density. --- With the angle-stabilized network and the authors' dense starting geometry (3.0 rods per σ², a 12σ-thick slab), the model cleanly separates a reproducible elastic modulus (about 3 in reduced units, ≈6 Pa) from a reproducible remodelling time (about 40–60 in reduced time units); forming-and-breaking and forming-only crosslinking agree at about 2.6 crosslinks per rod, so the value is well defined where both were previously noise-limited. As the crosslink fraction rises, the modulus climbs through the published ≈0.03 Pa near the percolation point (around 0.8 crosslinks per rod) and reaches about 8 Pa when saturated — so the published softness is a sparse-crosslink state, not a gap in the model, and the apparent large discrepancy with the paper disappears.
decisions_needed: Reproduction conventions: the article alone does not fix every convention needed to reproduce it. Acquire the supplemental tissue-model equations and the precise Figure 1 parameter values.

Released turnover kinetics: pin down the grand-canonical monomer exchange, the distance-gated breaking, the 7S-specific mechanics, and the original stress-to-energy conversion before freezing the collagen reference.
Collagen supply law: a fixed concentration (for reproducing the paper) or a secretion flux (for the lumenoid hypothesis). Decide per study.
3D calibration data: obtain lumenoid geometry over time, cell height and volume, membrane thickness, and collagen-versus-laminin staining before calibrating the 3D models.
Actin fidelity: use a validated reduced cortical model unless a molecularly-resolved actin cortex changes a measurable prediction. An explicit go/no-go call.

Composite modularity: keep the collagen-network composites as thin selections over one general, parameterized network builder (chemistry, bending stiffness, density, and strain protocol as configuration), rather than near-duplicate generators.

Absolute modulus in pascals: the angle-stabilized model reproduces the published ≈0.03 Pa and gives a reproducible modulus in reduced units (E ≈ 3 LJ). An exact value in pascals additionally needs the released monomer exchange, the distance-gated 7S break (0.95), and the dense starting configuration — or accept the reduced-unit value and settle the energy-scale choice below.
Engine for the early stages: LAMMPS now, with Smoldyn revisited when surface binders are added.
Energy scale: report the modulus in pascals (fit to a measured modulus) or keep kT units and report a ratio.
Coupling contract: which vertex-model term receives the membrane — a basal tension, a mobility, or an elastic spring.
Linker values: density, spring constant, and off-rate; sweep the off-rate as a multiple of the crosslink break rate.
Growth rate: extract ε̇ from the lumenoid radius over time (still needed).
Slab thickness and layer count (one z-stack away).
Which readout calibrates and which validates: the remodelling time calibrates the formation probability and the time unit, so it cannot also validate.

studies.name: bm-v1-stage1-modulus-remodelling
studies.title: Elastic modulus & remodelling-time separation
studies.question: Can the clean-room collagen IV network separate an elastic modulus from a viscous remodelling time, as the paper's staged protocol does?

resolved_uncertainties: The viscous 'relaxation' densification was a fix-bond/break artifact — root-caused and fixed.
The ~0 modulus is rigidity-percolation physics (z < 4), not a measurement failure.
remaining_uncertainties: τ (remodelling time) — below detection until the network is rigid.
Absolute modulus in pascals — energy scale still open (spec #4).

followup_study_proposals.title: Off-rate → τ calibration to the ≈20 h lifetime

findings.statement: LAMMPS `fix bond/break` models only OVER-STRETCH breaking, not a force- independent off-rate — small Rmax dissolves the network, large Rmax saturates it. Replacing it with a controlled random-deletion off-rate gives a make/break steady state and crosslink turnover.

evidence.observed: crosslinks 45→401 (old, densifies) vs steady ~54 then decay 46→3 (off-rate)

findings.explanation: Breaking must be length-independent to be a controllable rate (spec: force-independent in v1).
findings.next_action: adopted in viva_lumenoid/collagen.py; guarded by a regression test

findings.statement: The v1 central-force network is below the 2D rigidity threshold (mean z ≤ 3 < 4), so its elastic modulus is statistically consistent with zero — matching the published ≈0.03 Pa.

evidence.observed: modulus −0.03 ± 0.06 LJ (95% CI, 6 seeds); mean z ≈ 1.2; z_max = 3

findings.explanation: Maxwell counting: NC1 beads reach z = 2, 7S beads z = 4, mean ≤ 3 < 4 → floppy regardless of crosslink density. (Scoped to the ANGLE-OFF transcription; the released model carries junction angles and is soft for other reasons — bm-v3.)

findings.statement: The remodelling mechanism is now correct (stress decays as crosslinks break), but the relaxable stress is small in a floppy network, so τ is below detection at v1 scale.

evidence.observed: ensemble viscous decay ~0.29→0.25; s0 < 2·noise → τ unresolved

findings.next_action: resolve on a rigid (bending) network or a much larger ensemble

studies.claim: A coarse-grained collagen IV network (two-bead rods, stochastic NC1/7S crosslinks, no excluded volume) run through the spec's stage-1 protocol — stretch, hold, then switch the chemistry on — yields a separable elastic modulus and remodelling (stress-relaxation) time on real LAMMPS.

biological_validation.basis: Consistent with the published ≈0.03 Pa (near-floppy) modulus; the floppiness is mechanistically explained by connectivity (z < 4).

regression_compatibility.basis: No upstream regression baseline for this clean-room build.

explanatory_gain.basis: Identifies WHY the BM network is soft — connectivity below rigidity percolation — telling the vertex model that BM stiffness comes from bending/bundling, not crosslink count.

derived.insight: LAMMPS `fix bond/break` models only OVER-STRETCH breaking, not a force- independent off-rate — small Rmax dissolves the network, large Rmax saturates it. Replacing it with a controlled random-deletion off-rate gives a make/break steady state and crosslink turnover.

key_metrics.label: elastic-modulus-consistent-with-floppy

key_metrics.label: relaxation-decays-not-densifies

studies.name: bm-v2-stress-vs-strainrate
studies.title: Growth rheology: stress vs strain rate
studies.question: What is σ(ε̇), and where does the network cross from viscous to elastic?
studies.claim: Imposing an equibiaxial in-plane strain rate ε̇ on the growing collagen IV network and reading the steady-state stress σ(ε̇) gives the effective viscosity η = σ/ε̇ (viscous at slow rates) and the rate at which the response turns elastic — the σ(ε̇) relation a vertex model needs.

key_metrics.label: sweep-runs
key_metrics.value: σ and η returned for every rate in the ε̇ sweep

key_metrics.label: viscosity-defined
key_metrics.value: low-rate effective viscosity computed (elastic-dominated at these rates)

studies.name: bm-v3-junction-bending-rigidity
studies.title: Rigidity percolation (central-force control)
studies.question: Can more crosslink connectivity rigidify the v1 network, or is bending required?

findings.statement: Raising NC1/7S crosslink caps lifts measured z only to ~2.0 (never near the z = 4 threshold), and the modulus stays consistent with zero throughout — central-force connectivity cannot rigidify the v1 angle-off sheet.

evidence.observed: z 1.24→2.03 (angles off, corrected params); modulus consistent with 0

expected.range: rigid only for z ≥ 4 (2D central-force isostatic point)

findings.explanation: NC1×1 + 7S×3 caps z at ~3 in principle, but the sparse angle-off geometry only reaches z≈2.0; either way it saturates below 4.
findings.next_action: implement junction bending (released NC1/7S angles) — carried out in bm-v4

studies.claim: This study originally explained the soft modulus as a central-force rigidity-percolation effect (z ≤ 3 < 4). The released code is not a central-force network — it sets junction angles (NC1 at 180° with stiffness 4.0, 7S at 155° and 60°) — so that explanation does not describe the published model, which carries those angles and is still soft (≈0.03 Pa). What this connectivity sweep actually shows is that with angles off (our earlier transcription) and the corrected parameters, the network is sub-isostatic (z tops out at ≈2.0) and soft — a property of the angle-off transcription, not of the paper.

derived.insight: Raising NC1/7S crosslink caps lifts measured z only to ~2.0 (never near the z = 4 threshold), and the modulus stays consistent with zero throughout — central-force connectivity cannot rigidify the v1 angle-off sheet.

key_metrics.label: modulus-stays-floppy
key_metrics.value: modulus consistent with 0 at every rung (angles off)

studies.name: bm-v4-junction-bending
studies.title: Native junction-bending modulus
studies.question: Does junction bending yield the measurable modulus the vertex model needs?

resolved_uncertainties: Bending, not crosslink connectivity, governs this network's stiffness (confirmed qualitatively).
The athermal minimisation measures the floppy modulus deterministically (removes the dynamic-measurement noise).
A reproducible, positive bending modulus IS obtained with real angles created during assembly (36.7/27.6/37.5 LJ) — the as-formed-restraint ill-conditioning was an artifact, not an intrinsic limit.
remaining_uncertainties: The ABSOLUTE (Pa) modulus — blocked on matching the released make+break crosslink density (GCE) and the energy-scale decision (#4).

followup_study_proposals.title: Absolute bending modulus by matching the released make+break density (GCE)

findings.statement: Junction bending is implemented as `fix restrain` pinned to each junction's as-formed angle (per-junction rest angle avoids the single-rest-angle frustration), with an auto-reduced timestep and an athermal energy-minimised modulus readout.

evidence.observed: floppy modulus measured as E ≈ 0 (deterministic) via minimisation

findings.statement: The AS-FORMED restraint path — bending pinned via `fix restrain` AFTER assembly — is ill-conditioned at v1 size: |E| jumps to tens–hundreds but scatters and sign-flips across seeds (k=80 per-seed −570…+54, median −210), so it yields no calibratable value. SUPERSEDED by F3: the ill-conditioning was an artifact of applying bending after assembly, not an intrinsic limit.
findings.explanation: The stiff, pre-stressed, disordered small network has many near-degenerate energy minima; the equibiaxial-stress modulus is dominated by pre-stress and finite-size buckling rather than the intrinsic shear modulus. Creating the angles DURING assembly (F3) lets the network equilibrate compatible with them and removes this pathology.
findings.next_action: superseded — see F3 (real angles during assembly)

findings.statement: Creating real harmonic angles as the crosslinks form (use_real_angles, matching the released bond/react templates) yields a POSITIVE, well- conditioned, reproducible modulus — per-seed 36.7/27.6/37.5 LJ (same sign, tight IQR). So the released model is not floppy once its angles are faithfully active; the modulus is finite and strongly density-dependent (≈79 Pa at 2.9 crosslinks/rod → ≈7 Pa at 1.0/rod).

evidence.observed: real angles during assembly: per-seed 36.7/27.6/37.5 LJ; reproducible=true

findings.explanation: Equilibrating the network WITH the angles active (rather than pinning them on afterwards) removes the pre-stress / near-degenerate-minima pathology of F2. The remaining gap for an absolute Pa value is matching the released make+break crosslink density (the make-only real-angle path over-crosslinks), which needs per-angle deletion or the GCE, plus the energy-scale decision (#4).
findings.next_action: match the released dense make+break crosslink density (GCE) for an absolute modulus

studies.claim: Junction bending is a released feature (an NC1 angle of stiffness 4.0 at 180°, plus 7S angles), not a new ingredient; how it is applied decides whether it gives a usable modulus. Pinning as-formed restraints on after assembly is ill-conditioned — the sign flips and no reproducible value emerges. Creating real harmonic angles as the crosslinks form, so the network equilibrates with them active (matching the released bond/react templates), gives a positive, well-conditioned, reproducible modulus. The released model is not floppy once its angles are active; its modulus is finite and strongly density-dependent.

derived.insight: Junction bending is implemented as `fix restrain` pinned to each junction's as-formed angle (per-junction rest angle avoids the single-rest-angle frustration), with an auto-reduced timestep and an athermal energy-minimised modulus readout.

key_metrics.label: bending-changes-mechanics

findings.statement: The NC1/7S-only topology does not bundle: mean strand size stays near 1 (~82% singletons), below the 5–7 protomers per strand measured in the PFHR-9 scaffold. The model has no lateral-association bond.

findings.explanation: The released model bundles only through 7S branching; the lateral- association bond that builds strands is absent (spec: a lateral term would itself under-bundle ~2× if calibrated in vitro).

studies.claim: Of the two geometric readouts the model should reproduce, one is met and one is not. The simulated pore-size distribution reaches the measured corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at realistic density, while the protomers-per-strand distribution stays near 1, below the measured 5-7. The released NC1/7S topology has no lateral-association bond, so it cannot form multi-protomer strands — a limitation identified in advance.
